name: Guiding VLM Agents with Process Rewards at Inference Time for GUI Navigation
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.
summary: Guides visual GUI agents at inference time with a process-reward model that evaluates intermediate actions. It combines stepwise guidance with trajectory reflection and retry mechanisms in static and interactive navigation tasks.

name: PixelWeb: The First Web GUI Dataset with Pixel-Wise Labels
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.
summary: Introduces PixelWeb, a webpage GUI dataset with element images, contours, and pixel masks. Its annotation pipeline combines bitmap channel information with DOM-based visibility and stacking analysis to address occlusion and overlapping elements.

name: ScaleTrack: Scaling and back-tracking Automated GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: ScaleTrack combines a unified collection of GUI grounding samples with a planning objective that predicts the next action while reconstructing prior actions. This backward prediction links the current screenshot to interaction history during agent training.

name: Visual Test-time Scaling for GUI Agent Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: RegionFocus adds visual test-time scaling by zooming into selected screenshot regions and maintaining an image-based map of landmarks and actions. It evaluates this grounding procedure with UI-TARS and Qwen2.5-VL on ScreenSpot-Pro and WebVoyager.

name: Leveraging Vision-Language Models for Visual Grounding and Analysis of Automotive UI
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). Automotive interfaces are the primary setting; ScreenSpot is reported as a separate cross-domain evaluation.
summary: Introduces AutomotiveUI-Bench-4K and a fine-tuned vision-language model for locating elements and evaluating automotive infotainment interfaces.

name: Enhancing Visual Grounding for GUI Agents via Self-Evolutionary Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Proposes GUI grounding training that combines curated seed examples, continuous location-dependent policy feedback, and iterative refinement guided by attention maps. The study evaluates the resulting reinforcement-learning procedure on three grounding benchmarks, including ScreenSpot-Pro.

name: GUI-Shift: Enhancing VLM-Based GUI Agents through Self-supervised Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUI-Shift trains an inverse-dynamics task that predicts the initial action connecting two GUI states, using trajectories without natural-language instructions. It combines rule-based reinforcement learning with data filtering and evaluates transfer to Android automation and screenshot grounding.

name: Scaling Computer-Use Grounding via User Interface Decomposition and Synthesis
notes: Summary and topic tags reviewed against the primary abstract.
summary: Introduces OSWorld-G grounding evaluation and the Jedi synthesis pipeline for examples spanning layout reasoning and fine-grained interaction.

name: ReGUIDE: Data Efficient GUI Grounding via Spatial Reasoning and Search
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Combines self-generated localization reasoning, spatial consistency checks, and inference-time search to improve data-efficient web grounding.

name: GUI-G1: Understanding R1-Zero-Like Training for Visual Grounding in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Analyzes reasoning templates, reward design, and policy updates in GUI grounding, then proposes targeted adjustments to the training process.

name: TransBench: Breaking Barriers for Transferable Graphical User Interface Agents in Dynamic Digital Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces TransBench to evaluate GUI grounding transfer across app versions, iOS, Android, Web, and functionally distinct applications.

name: XBOUND: Exploring Capability Boundaries of Device-Control Agents at the State Level
notes: Reviewed against the complete official arXiv abstract.
summary: XBOUND evaluates GUI agents at the level of a screen state, considering multiple instructions and possible target actions within it. The study separates action matching from instruction unification and compares effects of grounding and trajectory data.

name: Grounded Reinforcement Learning for Visual Reasoning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). GUI localization is one part of a broader visual reasoning evaluation.
summary: Introduces ViGoRL, a visual reasoning model trained to reference image coordinates and zoom during reasoning; its evaluations include GUI element localization.

name: Surfer-H Meets Holo1: Cost-Efficient Web Agent Powered by Open Weights
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Describes Surfer-H, a web agent paired with the Holo1 vision-language model family trained on web content, synthetic examples, and agent-generated data. The work introduces WebClick for web-interface localization and evaluates browser task execution on WebVoyager.

name: GUI-Actor: Coordinate-Free Visual Grounding for GUI Agents
notes: Editorial summary based on the primary paper abstract.
summary: Uses an attention-based action head and a verifier to select relevant screen regions without generating coordinates as text.

name: MiMo-VL Technical Report
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). GUI grounding is one application within a broader multimodal model report.
summary: Reports MiMo-VL-7B-SFT and MiMo-VL-7B-RL, general vision-language models trained with staged pre-training and mixed RL, with GUI grounding evaluated on OSWorld-G.

name: LPO: Towards Accurate GUI Agent Interaction via Location Preference Optimization
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Location Preference Optimization uses an information-entropy signal to select interaction regions and a distance-based reward to assess click locations. It trains GUI localization through preference optimization and evaluates both offline grounding and online interaction.

name: UITron-Speech: Towards Automated GUI Agents Based on Speech Instructions
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces UITron-Speech, which predicts GUI actions from spoken instructions and screenshots. It combines synthetic speech data and mixed-modality training with a training-free grounding refinement step.

name: Understanding GUI Agent Localization Biases through Logit Sharpness
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: Introduces a finer-grained taxonomy of GUI localization errors and a logit-based Peak Sharpness Score for analyzing coordinate-prediction uncertainty. A context-aware cropping method refines the visual input without retraining the grounding model.

name: Learning, Reasoning, Refinement: A Framework for Kahneman's Dual-System Intelligence in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: CogniGUI combines hierarchical visual parsing of interface elements with a GRPO-based grounding agent that compares alternative interaction paths. Its ScreenSeek benchmark evaluates navigation across applications, changing interface states, and consistency between interfaces.

name: ZonUI-3B: A Lightweight Vision-Language Model for Cross-Resolution GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: ZonUI-3B trains GUI grounding with a curated 24,000-example collection of mobile, desktop, and web screenshots. Its two-stage procedure first learns across platforms and then specializes on high-resolution images, with ablations on data diversity and redundant examples.

name: DiMo-GUI: Advancing Test-time Scaling in GUI Grounding via Modality-Aware Visual Reasoning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Separates textual and iconic UI elements and iteratively focuses visual regions to refine grounding without additional model training.

name: R-VLM: Region-Aware Vision Language Model for Precise GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: R-VLM localizes GUI elements through zoomed-in region proposals and an intersection-over-union-aware training objective. It evaluates the grounding model on ScreenSpot and AgentStudio and studies its effect on navigation in AITW and Mind2Web.

name: GTA1: GUI Test-time Scaling Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GTA1 samples multiple action proposals at each GUI step and uses a judge to select among them. A separate grounding model is trained with reinforcement learning to map selected proposals to visual targets, linking planning-time search with click localization.

name: VisualTrap: A Stealthy Backdoor Attack on GUI Agents via Visual Grounding Manipulation
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies backdoors that redirect GUI visual grounding even when the task plan is correct. VisualTrap evaluates whether poisoned grounding training transfers to downstream tasks and across web, mobile, and desktop interface settings.

name: A Training-Free, Task-Agnostic Framework for Enhancing MLLM Performance on High-Resolution Images
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The method is task-agnostic and is also evaluated on 4K and 8K image perception.
summary: Introduces Extract Candidate then Predict (ECP), a training-free two-stage method for high-resolution images, evaluated partly on 4K GUI grounding.

name: LaSM: Layer-wise Scaling Mechanism for Defending Pop-up Attack on GUI Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces LaSM, a training-free defense that selectively scales attention and MLP components to improve alignment with task-relevant screen regions. It evaluates the approach against pop-up-based GUI injection attacks.

name: GUI-G$^2$: Gaussian Reward Modeling for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUI-G2 replaces binary grounding rewards with Gaussian point rewards and spatial-coverage rewards. An adaptive variance tied to element dimensions supplies continuous training feedback for targets of different sizes, evaluated on the ScreenSpot benchmark family.

name: MMBench-GUI: Hierarchical Multi-Platform Evaluation Framework for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: MMBench-GUI evaluates interface understanding, element grounding, task automation, and collaboration across six named desktop, mobile, and web platforms. It introduces the Efficiency-Quality Area metric for examining execution efficiency alongside task quality in online GUI automation.

name: UI-AGILE: Advancing GUI Agents with Effective Reinforcement Learning and Precise Inference-Time Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Combines grounding-oriented reward and sampling improvements with inference-time image decomposition and target selection.

name: Phi-Ground Tech Report: Advancing Perception in GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Reports a GUI-grounding model family and empirical design choices covering source data, perception training, and coordinate prediction.

name: Evolving in Tasks: Empowering the Multi-modality Large Language Model as the Computer Use Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: The Self-Evolution Agent combines automatic generation of verifiable computer-use trajectories with step-wise reinforcement learning for long-horizon training. It also describes a model-enhancement procedure that integrates grounding and planning capabilities without an additional training stage.

name: GuirlVG: Incentivize GUI Visual Grounding via Empirical Exploration on Reinforcement Learning
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.
summary: Introduces GuirlVG, an empirical study of reinforcement fine-tuning for GUI visual grounding. It analyzes training components and adds an adaptive KL-based mechanism to limit reward over-optimization.

name: Test-Time Reinforcement Learning for GUI Grounding via Region Consistency
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUI-RC aggregates multiple grounding predictions into spatial voting grids to choose a consensus region. GUI-RCPO then turns agreement with that region into a reward for test-time policy updates on unlabeled GUI screenshots.

name: InfiGUI-G1: Advancing GUI Grounding with Adaptive Exploration Policy Optimization
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Uses multiple candidate answers and adaptive exploration rewards to improve spatial and semantic alignment in GUI grounding.

name: FineState-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Fine-Grained State Control in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: FineState-Bench evaluates fine-grained GUI perception and control across desktop, web, and mobile interfaces. Its Visual Diagnostic Assistant separates perception and localization contributions in controlled interaction experiments.

name: UI-Venus Technical Report: Building High-performance UI Agents with RFT
notes: Summary and topic tags reviewed against the primary abstract.
summary: Studies screenshot-based GUI grounding and navigation using curated interaction data, reward design, and reinforcement fine-tuning.

name: V2P: Visual Attention Calibration for GUI Grounding via Background Suppression and Center Peaking
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: V2P trains GUI grounding by suppressing attention to background regions and emphasizing the center of the target element. It represents target importance with size-dependent Gaussian heatmaps and evaluates the contribution of each component on ScreenSpot-v2 and ScreenSpot-Pro.

name: Structuring GUI Elements through Vision Language Models: Towards Action Space Generation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces IAML training, which augments coordinate samples to help multimodal models locate GUI elements from screen content and user instructions.

name: WebMMU: A Benchmark for Multimodal Multilingual Website Understanding and Code Generation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces WebMMU, a multilingual benchmark for website visual question answering, element grounding, code editing, and mockup-to-code generation.

name: WebSight: A Vision-First Architecture for Robust Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: WebSight uses a vision-language model trained on web-interface examples within a modular agent with planning, action, verification, and episodic memory components. It evaluates element clicking on Showdown Clicks and full browsing tasks on WebVoyager using visual observations.

publication.title: DashboardQA: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Question Answering on Interactive Dashboards
publication.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EACL 2026

name: DashboardQA: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Question Answering on Interactive Dashboards
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The benchmark centers on interactive dashboards from Tableau Public.
summary: Introduces DashboardQA to evaluate how vision-language GUI agents answer questions by interacting with dashboards, grounding elements, and planning actions.

name: SWIRL: A Staged Workflow for Interleaved Reinforcement Learning in Mobile GUI Control
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract also applies SWIRL to mathematical reasoning; the GUI application is mobile control.
summary: Introduces SWIRL, staged interleaved RL for mobile GUI control, pairing a Navigator that plans from screens and language with an Interactor that produces actions.

name: UItron: Foundational GUI Agent with Advanced Perception and Planning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: UItron combines GUI perception and planning data engineering with supervised training and curriculum reinforcement learning in connected mobile and PC environments. It also collects more than one million operation steps across 100 Chinese apps and builds offline and online evaluation environments.

name: AppCopilot: Toward General, Accurate, Long-Horizon, and Efficient Mobile Agent
notes: Trace reuse assumes stable layouts and fixed tasks. The described function-call routes are user-selected, and coordinate calibration depends on valid detected widgets. Basis: complete retained abstract and source-reviewed sections of the exact-version paper (4.2 OCR/OR Region Localization; 4.2.2 Coordinate Calibration; 4.3 Multi-Agent Voting; 5.2 Task Decomposition; 6.2 Experience Reuse; 6.3 Function Calling).
summary: Describes a mobile-agent stack combining region-based coordinate correction, hierarchical task planning, multi-agent voting, and reuse of successful interaction traces.

name: Learning Active Perception via Self-Evolving Preference Optimization for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: LASER builds preference data for multi-step GUI perception by combining Monte Carlo quality estimates with region-overlap evaluation. Its self-evolving training encourages relevant region selection and adapts the amount of reasoning before predicting screen coordinates.

name: SparkUI-Parser: Enhancing GUI Perception with Robust Grounding and Parsing
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.
summary: Introduces SparkUI-Parser, which adds continuous coordinate decoding and a rejection mechanism for nonexistent targets to a multimodal model. It also presents ScreenParse for evaluating structural interface perception.

name: How Auxiliary Reasoning Unleashes GUI Grounding in VLMs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Studies the gap between latent visual grounding and explicit coordinate output in general vision-language models. Three zero-shot methods add axes, grids, or labeled intersections to GUI screenshots so models can express spatial locations without fine-tuning.

name: See, Think, Act: Teaching Multimodal Agents to Effectively Interact with GUI by Identifying Toggles
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.
summary: Introduces a benchmark for binary GUI-toggle instructions and State-aware Reasoning, which compares the observed control state with the requested state before choosing an action. It evaluates agents on toggle tasks and broader interactive benchmarks.

name: GUI-ARP: Enhancing Grounding with Adaptive Region Perception for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUI-ARP uses visual attention to crop relevant screenshot regions and decides whether a target needs single-stage or multi-stage analysis. Supervised fine-tuning followed by GRPO trains this adaptive procedure for high-resolution GUI grounding.

name: BTL-UI: Blink-Think-Link Reasoning Model for GUI Agent
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: BTL-UI separates GUI interaction into screen-region attention, planning and executable-command generation. It adds an automated annotation pipeline and rule-based process/outcome rewards for training, with evaluation on both static understanding and dynamic interaction.

name: UIPro: Unleashing Superior Interaction Capability For GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: UIPro pretrains GUI understanding on 20.6 million tasks and then harmonizes interaction datasets through a unified action space. Continued fine-tuning uses the merged multi-platform data to train action prediction for generalist GUI operation.

name: Learning GUI Grounding with Spatial Reasoning from Visual Feedback
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: GUI-Cursor treats GUI grounding as a sequence of cursor movements guided by visible feedback and movement history. Online reinforcement learning with trajectory rewards trains the model to refine the target location across multiple steps.

name: Generalist Scanner Meets Specialist Locator: A Synergistic Coarse-to-Fine Framework for Robust GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: GMS pairs a general vision-language scanner that proposes interface regions with a specialist locator that predicts coordinates within them. Hierarchical coarse-to-fine search coordinates the two components for GUI grounding on ScreenSpot-Pro.

name: Ferret-UI Lite: Lessons from Building Small On-Device GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Ferret-UI Lite develops a 3B GUI agent using mixed real and synthetic data, reasoning with visual tools at inference, and reinforcement learning. It evaluates grounding and navigation across mobile, web, and desktop settings, including AndroidWorld and OSWorld.

name: Improving GUI Grounding with Explicit Position-to-Coordinate Mapping
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: This work addresses GUI localization errors caused by mismatches between visual patch positions and output pixel coordinates. RULER tokens provide explicit coordinate references, while Interleaved MRoPE balances width and height encoding; evaluation uses the ScreenSpot benchmark family.

name: \textsc{GUI-Spotlight}: Adaptive Iterative Focus Refinement for Enhanced GUI Visual Grounding
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: GUI-Spotlight trains a grounding model to reason over images and call tools that iteratively narrow its visual focus. The paper evaluates this refinement method on ScreenSpot-Pro after training on 18,500 samples.

name: Detect Anything via Next Point Prediction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). GUI grounding is one evaluated capability of a general visual perception model.
summary: Introduces Rex-Omni, a general visual perception model trained for coordinate prediction; GUI grounding is one capability evaluated alongside detection and OCR.

name: AndroidControl-Curated: Revealing the True Potential of GUI Agents through Benchmark Purification
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: AndroidControl-Curated audits ambiguities and factual errors in AndroidControl and produces a refined evaluation dataset. The paper also studies post-training a small Magma-R1 model on a curated subset to examine the effect of data quality on GUI action assessment.

name: UI-Ins: Enhancing GUI Grounding with Multi-Perspective Instruction-as-Reasoning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Treats alternative instruction formulations as reasoning paths and trains GUI-grounding models to select and combine useful perspectives.

name: Mixing Importance with Diversity: Joint Optimization for KV Cache Compression in Large Vision-Language Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). GUI grounding is one evaluation setting for a general vision-language model compression method.
summary: MixKV compresses vision-language model KV caches by balancing importance and diversity; its evaluations include GUI grounding alongside broader multimodal tasks.

name: Enhancing Trustworthy GUI Grounding via Self-Critiqued Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: HyperClick trains GUI grounders to produce a click and an accompanying confidence estimate using rewards for correctness and confidence alignment. Its evaluation examines localization, calibration, and abstention behavior.

name: GUI-AIMA: Aligning Intrinsic Multimodal Attention with a Context Anchor for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces GUI-AIMA, which supervises instruction-relevant attention over visual patches. Patch-level grounding can be combined with an optional zoom stage and is evaluated across GUI localization benchmarks.

name: GUI-360$^\circ$: A Comprehensive Dataset and Benchmark for Computer-Using Agents
notes: Summary and topic tags reviewed against the primary abstract.
summary: Collects Windows application trajectories with screenshots and action traces for grounding, screen parsing, and action prediction.

name: AUTO-Explorer: Automated Data Collection for GUI Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces Auto-Explorer, an automated GUI exploration method that records software states for training-data collection. UIXplore evaluates exploration coverage, and collected data is used to fine-tune and test GUI element grounding.

name: Grounding Computer Use Agents on Human Demonstrations
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: GroundCUA turns expert desktop demonstrations into densely annotated screenshots and grounding instructions. The GroundNext model family uses this supervision and subsequent reinforcement learning, with both grounding benchmarks and an OSWorld agent configuration used for evaluation.

name: An Efficient Training Pipeline for Reasoning Graphical User Interface Agents
notes: Training compares supervised fine-tuning, chain-of-thought-augmented fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning through Group Relative Policy Optimization. The authors report that models trained on the filtered data match or surpass larger baselines.
summary: A GUI grounding pipeline filters 4.8M synthetic examples to 12K training instances and adapts a 3B vision-language model, evaluated on ScreenSpot, Multimodal-Mind2Web, and AndroidControl.

name: Co-EPG: A Framework for Co-Evolution of Planning and Grounding in Autonomous GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: Co-EPG alternates reinforcement learning for a planner with updates to a grounding model using generated training examples. The evolving grounder provides feedback to the planner, and evaluation uses Multimodal Mind2Web and AndroidControl.

name: MEGA-GUI: Multi-stage Enhanced Grounding Agents for GUI Elements
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces MEGA-GUI, which separates coarse region selection from fine-grained interface-element grounding. Bidirectional zooming and context-aware instruction rewriting coordinate specialized vision-language agents across visual scales.

name: Prune4Web: DOM Tree Pruning Programming for Web Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces Prune4Web, where generated scoring programs filter DOM elements according to decomposed subtasks before grounding. An annotation pipeline and two-turn training procedure coordinate the planner, programmatic filter and grounder.

name: AFRAgent : An Adaptive Feature Renormalization Based High Resolution Aware GUI agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces AFRAgent, which uses adaptive feature renormalization to combine low-resolution visual embeddings with high-resolution details. The architecture is evaluated for smartphone GUI automation on Meta-GUI and AITW.

name: DrawingBench: Evaluating Spatial Reasoning and UI Interaction Capabilities of Large Language Models through Mouse-Based Drawing Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: DrawingBench evaluates sequences of low-level mouse-based GUI actions through 250 drawing prompts and rule-based criteria. Action inspection and multi-turn external feedback support analysis of spatial reasoning, tool-state management, and refinement.

name: Chain-of-Ground: Improving GUI Grounding via Iterative Reasoning and Reference Feedback
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: Chain-of-Ground uses iterative visual reasoning and reference feedback to refine GUI localization without additional training. It evaluates on ScreenSpot-Pro and introduces TPanel-UI to probe grounding on industrial control panels with visual distortions.

name: Zoom in, Click out: Unlocking and Evaluating the Potential of Zooming for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: ZoomClick uses repeated zooming and context adjustment to improve GUI grounding without training. The paper studies zoom depth, crop sizes, and related choices and introduces GUIZoom-Bench to evaluate how grounding models respond to zoomed views.

name: MVP: Multiple View Prediction Improves GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: MVP addresses unstable GUI coordinates by predicting across several attention-guided cropped views. It clusters the resulting coordinates and selects the densest cluster centroid, evaluating this training-free inference method across grounding models.

name: VenusBench-GD: A Comprehensive Multi-Platform GUI Benchmark for Diverse Grounding Tasks
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: VenusBench-GD is a bilingual, cross-platform GUI grounding benchmark organized into basic and advanced tasks. Its annotation pipeline and six-subtask taxonomy support comparisons of general multimodal models and GUI-specialized models across different grounding demands.

name: DAVE: A VLM Vision Encoder for Document Understanding and Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: DAVE trains a vision encoder for document images and web agents using self-supervised pretraining followed by supervised parsing and localization. It combines decoder-specific encoder merging with feature fusion and evaluates web localization and agent benchmarks alongside document tasks.

name: iSHIFT: Lightweight Slow-Fast GUI Agent with Adaptive Perception
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces iSHIFT, which combines latent reasoning with perception-control tokens to adapt GUI inference. The agent switches between detailed regional grounding and faster use of global visual cues.

name: ShowUI-$π$: Flow-based Generative Models as GUI Dexterous Hands
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Models discrete clicks and continuous drags with flow-based action generation, and introduces drag trajectories and the ScreenDrag benchmark.

name: FocusUI: Efficient UI Grounding via Position-Preserving Visual Token Selection
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: FocusUI selects instruction-relevant screenshot patches while preserving their positional structure for GUI grounding. Its PosPad scheme replaces runs of dropped tokens with positional markers and is evaluated under reduced token budgets.

name: Beyond Clicking:A Step Towards Generalist GUI Grounding via Text Dragging
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The dataset and benchmark focus on dragging to select and manipulate text.
summary: GUI-Drag provides synthesized text-dragging examples, while ScreenDrag benchmarks selecting text by dragging across varied GUI contexts.

name: GUI-Eyes: Tool-Augmented Perception for Visual Grounding in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: GUI-Eyes trains GUI grounders to decide when and how to use visual tools such as crops and zooms. Its coarse-to-fine policy uses dense spatial rewards based on location proximity and region overlap, with evaluation on ScreenSpot-Pro.

name: Compress to Focus: Efficient Coordinate Compression for Policy Optimization in Multi-Turn GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: CCPO couples GUI policy optimization with coordinate-guided compression of past visual observations. It aggregates targets across rollouts to focus retained context and uses distance-based advantages to train grounding and compression together.

name: GUIGuard-Bench: Toward a General Evaluation for Privacy-Preserving GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces GUIGuard-Bench, which annotates private regions in GUI trajectories with categories, risk levels, and relevance to the user’s task. It evaluates privacy recognition and the effect of screenshot protection on offline planning and task utility.

name: MAGNET: Towards Adaptive GUI Agents with Memory-Driven Knowledge Evolution
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MAGNET maintains separate memories for stable interface functions and task procedures across changing layouts and workflows. It updates frequently used knowledge and evaluates adaptation in AndroidWorld and offline distribution-shift settings.

name: OmegaUse: Building a General-Purpose GUI Agent for Autonomous Task Execution
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: OmegaUse combines exploratory and taxonomy-guided data synthesis with supervised fine-tuning followed by GRPO for GUI control. The report introduces OS-Nav for offline Android and Ubuntu evaluation alongside established grounding and action-prediction benchmarks.

name: Continual GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Continual GUI Agents defines grounding under changing application domains and screen resolutions. Its GUI-AiF training framework uses separate point- and region-alignment rewards to adapt grounding as these distributions shift.

name: SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces SafeGround, which estimates GUI-grounding uncertainty from the spatial dispersion of sampled predictions and calibrates a decision threshold before testing. It studies risk-aware selection on ScreenSpot-Pro, with statistical control scoped to the threshold’s false-discovery rate.

name: Avenir-Web: Human-Experience-Imitating Multimodal Web Agents with Mixture of Grounding Experts
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Avenir-Web combines multiple grounding specialists with procedural experience, a task checklist and adaptive memory. It evaluates this planning and execution framework on live Online-Mind2Web tasks.

name: ToolTok: Tool Tokenization for Efficient and Generalizable GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: ToolTok represents GUI operations with learned tool tokens and frames interaction as progressive tool selection. Semantic anchoring and an easy-to-hard curriculum teach tool meanings before visual pathfinding, with evaluation across grounding scenarios.

name: Trifuse: Enhancing Attention-Based GUI Grounding via Multimodal Fusion
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Trifuse combines attention-based localization with OCR text cues and icon captions to ground GUI instructions. Its fusion procedure favors cross-modal agreement and sharp location peaks, and is evaluated without task-specific fine-tuning.

name: POINTS-GUI-G: GUI-Grounding Journey
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Studies GUI-grounding development from a weakly grounded base model through data preparation, visual training, and verifiable rewards.

name: GUI-GenBench: Evaluating Image Generation Models as Interactive GUI Environments
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: GUI-GenBench tests image-generation models as action-conditioned GUI environments across five suites, including transitions, trajectories and grounding. Its VLM-based GUI-Score separates goal completion, interaction logic, consistency and visual properties.

name: UI-Venus-1.5 Technical Report
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Describes a GUI-agent family combining broad intermediate training, full-trajectory online reinforcement learning, and merging of specialized models.

name: See, Plan, Snap: Evaluating Multimodal GUI Agents in Scratch
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: ScratchWorld evaluates program construction through the Scratch interface using fine-grained drag-and-drop actions and a complementary semantic-API mode. Runtime tests assess the resulting programs, allowing analysis of the gap between program reasoning and GUI manipulation.

name: Building Autonomous GUI Navigation via Agentic-Q Estimation and Step-Wise Policy Optimization
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This framework learns an agentic-Q model to estimate individual actions’ contributions to GUI task completion. It then optimizes a policy with step-level samples from its own trajectories, decoupling policy updates from environment interaction.

name: ScreenParse: Moving Beyond Sparse Grounding with Complete Screen Parsing Supervision
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: ScreenParse supplies dense annotations of UI elements, types and text in web screenshots through an automated rendering and filtering pipeline. ScreenVLM learns to output structured screen markup, and the study evaluates dense parsing and transfer to GUI grounding.

name: GUI-Libra: Training Native GUI Agents to Reason and Act with Action-aware Supervision and Partially Verifiable RL
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: GUI-Libra trains GUI agents with action-aware supervision, a curated reasoning dataset and reinforcement learning adapted to partially verifiable actions across web and mobile tasks.

name: Spatio-Temporal Token Pruning for Efficient High-Resolution GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: GUIPruner compresses high-resolution screenshots and interaction history for GUI navigation through training-free resizing and layout-aware token pruning.

name: WebChain: A Large-Scale Human-Annotated Dataset of Real-World Web Interaction Traces
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: WebChain aligns human web-interaction trajectories with visual, structural and action data for agent training. It also introduces WebChainBench and a mid-training approach that separates spatial grounding from planning.

name: Adaptive Vision-Language Model Routing for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Adaptive VLM Routing estimates GUI-action difficulty and small-model confidence to select a model under a predicted reliability threshold. Grounding and agent-routing benchmarks assess the cost–accuracy trade-off, with prior interaction context used for warm agents.

name: Zoom to Essence: Trainless GUI Grounding by Inferring upon Interface Elements
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Presents ZoomUI, a training-free grounding method that expresses instructions as visual element descriptions and uses model attention to zoom progressively into relevant interface regions. Evaluation examines instruction-to-element localization on GUI benchmarks.

name: Visual Confused Deputy: Exploiting and Defending Perception Failures in Computer-Using Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Formalizes a visual confused-deputy failure in which a computer agent acts on a misperceived UI object. A separate guardrail checks both the visual target and the agent's action reasoning against deployment-specific knowledge before permitting execution.

name: AdaZoom-GUI: Adaptive Zoom-based GUI Grounding with Instruction Refinement
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Combines instruction rewriting with conditional second-stage zooming for small GUI targets. A grounding dataset and GRPO training support joint prediction of click coordinates and element bounding boxes.

name: MedSPOT: A Workflow-Aware Sequential Grounding Benchmark for Clinical GUI
notes: Editorial summary based on the primary paper abstract.
summary: Benchmarks sequential target localization in clinical software workflows, emphasizing how early mistakes affect subsequent interaction steps.

name: CUA-Suite: Massive Human-annotated Video Demonstrations for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: CUA-Suite combines continuous expert desktop demonstrations in VideoCUA with the UI-Vision evaluation benchmark and GroundCUA grounding data. Screen recordings, cursor traces and layered annotations support study of temporal behavior and professional software workflows.

name: Towards GUI Agents: Vision-Language Diffusion Models for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Adapts a discrete vision-language diffusion model to single-turn GUI action and bounding-box prediction, using a hybrid masking schedule for coordinate geometry. Experiments across web, desktop and mobile datasets examine grounding accuracy and inference tradeoffs.

name: GUIDE: Resolving Domain Bias in GUI Agents through Real-Time Web Video Retrieval and Plug-and-Play Annotation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: GUIDE retrieves relevant software tutorials through subtitle-based video search, then infers planning and grounding knowledge from consecutive annotated keyframes. It inserts that knowledge into existing GUI-agent modules without parameter updates and evaluates the plug-in on OSWorld.

name: MolmoPoint: Better Pointing for VLMs with Grounding Tokens
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent general VLM pointing method with an explicit GUI-grounding experiment; no autonomous GUI-task execution is established.
summary: MolmoPoint replaces textual coordinate generation with pointing tokens that select visual regions and refine them through subpatches. The general image/video method includes GUI-pointing evaluation on ScreenSpotPro alongside other visual grounding tasks.

name: What's Missing in Screen-to-Action? Towards a UI-in-the-Loop Paradigm for Multimodal GUI Reasoning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces UILoop, which inserts explicit UI-element localization, function and usage reasoning between screen observation and action. UI Comprehension-Bench evaluates these element-level capabilities with three metrics.

name: Are GUI Agents Focused Enough? Automated Distraction via Semantic-level UI Element Injection
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This study tests black-box GUI-grounding failures caused by strategically added, innocuous-looking UI elements. Its iterative overlay search is compared with random injection and repeated independent grounding trials to distinguish persistent misdirection from incidental clutter.

name: Avenir-UX: Automated UX Evaluation via Simulated Human Web Interaction with GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Avenir-UX combines grounded web interaction with simulated user profiles and structured usability measures to produce evaluations of website journeys. The paper describes its architecture and use of SUS, step-wise ease questions and think-aloud traces for automated UX reporting.

name: PrecisionCUA: Iterative Visual Refinement for Pixel-Precise Cursor Grounding in Code Editors
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies iterative cursor grounding in dense code-editor interfaces, using visual feedback from earlier attempts to correct displacement. PrecisionCUA evaluates this closed-loop process across multiple model families on coding-interface tasks.

name: UI-Zoomer: Uncertainty-Driven Adaptive Zoom-In for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces UI-Zoomer, a training-free grounding method that uses candidate agreement and token confidence to decide when to crop and retry. Prediction variance determines a separate crop radius for each uncertain interface target.

name: GUI-Perturbed: Domain Randomization Reveals Systematic Brittleness in GUI Grounding Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces GUI-Perturbed, which varies screenshot appearance and instruction wording independently to diagnose grounding failures. Experiments on three related model architectures examine relational instructions, browser zoom and augmentation-based fine-tuning.

name: Beyond Chat and Clicks: GUI Agents for In-Situ Assistance via Live Interface Transformation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: DOMSteer translates help requests and live page context into reversible DOM changes such as control highlighting, contextual tooltips and layout reorganization. The work evaluates in-place GUI assistance with interface tests, use cases and a comparative user study.

name: Zoom Consistency: A Free Confidence Signal in Multi-Step Visual Grounding Pipelines
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract describes model routing as a proof of concept and reports a small correlation with correctness.
summary: Proposes zoom consistency as a confidence signal for multistep GUI grounding and uses it to route between specialist and generalist visual grounding models.

name: HalluClear: Diagnosing, Evaluating and Mitigating Hallucinations in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces HalluClear with a GUI hallucination taxonomy, expert-calibrated evaluation workflow and structured-reasoning post-training scheme. It evaluates how these components affect hallucinations, grounding and action fidelity across GUI agents.

name: Measure Twice, Click Once: Co-evolving Proposer and Visual Critic via Reinforcement Learning for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Trains a GUI grounding proposer together with a visual critic that evaluates candidate locations rendered on screenshots. An adaptive reinforcement-learning schedule balances their development, using proposal diversity and critic feedback during training.

name: GoClick: Lightweight Element Grounding Model for Autonomous GUI Interaction
notes: Editorial summary based on the primary paper abstract.
summary: Studies a compact encoder-decoder grounding model and progressive training-data refinement for resource-constrained GUI interaction.

name: AutoGUI-v2: A Comprehensive Multi-Modal GUI Functionality Understanding Benchmark
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: AutoGUI-v2 evaluates interface functionality, grounding and predicted interaction outcomes using hierarchical regions derived through VLM-human annotation. Its tasks span multiple operating systems and expose differences between functional localization, captioning and transition-logic understanding.

name: FineState-Bench: Benchmarking State-Conditioned Grounding for Fine-grained GUI State Setting
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The benchmark measures exact target-state setting; the abstract reports low exact goal-state success.
summary: FineState-Bench tests whether GUI agents locate the intended control and set its exact state across desktop, web, and mobile interfaces, with stage-wise diagnostic metrics.

name: A11y-Compressor: A Framework for Enhancing the Efficiency of GUI Agent Observations through Visual Context Reconstruction and Redundancy Reduction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: A11y-Compressor transforms linearized accessibility trees through modal detection, redundancy reduction and semantic structuring. Its OSWorld evaluation measures both observation-token reduction and task success.

name: Learn where to Click from Yourself: On-Policy Self-Distillation for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: Introduces GUI-SD, an on-policy self-distillation method for locating GUI elements from instructions, using a visually enriched teacher context and entropy-guided token weighting.

name: AutoFocus: Uncertainty-Aware Active Visual Search for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Presents AutoFocus, a training-free grounding method that turns sampled coordinates and token uncertainty into spatial region proposals. Shape-aware crops and visual comparison select a target while retaining surrounding interface context.

name: X-OmniClaw Technical Report: A Unified Mobile Agent for Multimodal Understanding and Interaction
notes: The report presents demonstrations. Its behavior-cloning component captures runtime skills; literal trace replay is described as future work. No general benchmark result or release completeness is inferred. Basis: complete retained abstract and source-reviewed sections of the exact-version paper (2 Framework; 3 Omni Perception; 4 Omni Memory; 5.1 Omni Action in App Ecosystem; 5.2 Trajectory Cloned Execution).
summary: Describes an Android agent architecture combining multimodal perception, working and personal memory, hybrid XML/visual grounding, and reusable skills captured from user interactions.

name: BAMI: Training-Free Bias Mitigation in GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported accuracy change is measured on ScreenSpot-Pro.
summary: BAMI uses coarse-to-fine focus and candidate selection at inference time to address precision and ambiguity errors in GUI grounding.

name: Covering Human Action Space for Computer Use: Data Synthesis and Benchmark
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces CUActSpot to evaluate clicks, drags, drawing and other screen interactions across GUI, text, tables, canvases and natural images. A renderer-based pipeline records geometry and screenshots, then generates matching instructions and action traces for training a grounding model.

name: What Happens Before Decoding? Prefill Determines GUI Grounding in VLMs
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Re-Prefill adds an attention-guided second prefill pass that revisits candidate screen regions before coordinate generation. The study evaluates this training-free intervention across GUI-grounding models and benchmarks.

name: DRS-GUI: Dynamic Region Search for Training-Free GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: DRS-GUI searches screenshot regions through focus, shift and scatter operations selected by a tree-search planner. A region-quality reward guides this training-free perceptual search before final GUI grounding.

name: PAGER: Bridging the Semantic-Execution Gap in Point-Precise Geometric GUI Control
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces PAGE Bench for point-precise geometric GUI construction and PAGER, an agent that plans around primitive dependencies and executes pixel-level actions.

name: WinDeskGround: A Benchmark for Robust GUI Grounding in Complex Multi-Window Desktop Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: WinDeskGround synthesizes multi-window desktop layouts with controlled occlusion, density and semantic similarity to test GUI grounding robustness. Its instruction-target benchmark measures how localization changes when interfaces depart from simple single-layer scenes.

name: SE-GA: Memory-Augmented Self-Evolution for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: SE-GA retrieves hierarchical memories during inference and uses the collected experience in a separate policy-improvement pipeline. Its evaluation includes offline grounding/action tasks and online Android interaction, which measure different capabilities.

name: MUIAnno: An Expert-Annotated Dataset and Evaluation Benchmark for Mobile UI Understanding
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MUIAnno provides expert labels for elements in manually explored mobile-app screens, with a web annotation tool that emits structured JSON. It also supplies UI-element detection baselines for the dataset.

name: DocOS: Towards Proactive Document-Guided Actions in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: DocOS benchmarks agents that search online documentation and translate procedural instructions into GUI actions in interactive web environments. It separates failures to retrieve useful procedures from failures to ground retrieved instructions into executable actions.

name: CutVerse: A Compositional GUI Agents Benchmark for Media Post-Production Editing
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Cutverse benchmarks GUI agents on long editing workflows across professional media applications and parses recordings and input logs into grounded action trajectories.

name: GUI-C$^2$: Coarse-to-Fine GUI Grounding via Difficulty-Aware Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces GUI-D to score training samples by difficulty and GUI-C² to refine screen-element locations through area-gated cropping and reinforcement learning.

name: DragOn: A Benchmark and Dataset for Drag-Based GUI Interactions
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: DragOn supplies drag-grounding training data and a held-out benchmark for highlighting text, selecting cells, resizing elements and moving sliders. It evaluates existing vision-language models and a model fine-tuned on the drag tasks.

name: RunAgent SuperBrowser: A Theory of Autonomous Web Navigation Grounded in Human Browsing Behaviour
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: SUPERBROWSER combines screenshot-based target proposals with separate orchestration, planning and action roles. A bounded ledger and context-eviction process retain recent actions, task facts and checkpoints during browser execution.

name: GUI-AC: Enhancing Continual Learning in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: GUI-AC uses grounding certainty to adjust advantage weighting and policy-clipping bounds during continual reinforcement fine-tuning. Its mechanisms aim to suppress noisy confidence updates while retaining exploration under shifting GUI domains and resolutions.

name: A History-Aware Visually Grounded Critic for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: HiViG combines a compact history of completed actions with a visually grounded critic that checks proposed coordinates before execution. Its evaluations separate history-related planning failures from errors caused by targeting the wrong screen element.

name: Naive Visual Memory is Not Enough: A Failure-Mode Study of GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This study finds that full-image visual memory can reduce some state errors while worsening action-level failures. Its AGMem alternative stores local crops associated with successful actions or recovery and evaluates their use in desktop GUI tasks.

name: VISTA: View-Consistent Self-Verified Training for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: VISTA forms GRPO comparison groups from target-preserving crops of the same GUI instance with exactly remapped target boxes. A conditional, advantage-weighted cross-view anchor supplies additional supervision without entering the group baseline, and evaluation includes view-consistency robustness.

name: Trust the Right Teacher: Quality-Aware Self-Distillation for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Proposes quality-aware self-distillation for GUI coordinate generation under student-produced prefixes. A correctness-aware gate suppresses coordinate-token supervision outside the target box, while teacher-probability scaling adjusts the remaining signal strength.

name: Uncertainty Quantification for Computer-Use Agents: A Benchmark across Vision-Language Models and GUI Grounding Datasets
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Argus benchmarks post-hoc uncertainty methods for single-step GUI grounding across open-weight and closed-source observation regimes. It tests calibration, rejection, error severity and conformal click regions, finding that uncertainty rankings transfer less reliably across model/interface regimes than across datasets for one model.

name: WinDOM: Self-Family Distillation for Small-Model GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: WinDOM obtains bounding-box supervision from a Windows 11 web reimplementation driven through Playwright, and studies rejection-sampling distillation for small GUI grounders. It treats the depth of the supervised cold start as a GRPO choice, comparing same-size EMA and larger same-family teachers.

name: GUICrafter: Weakly-Supervised GUI Agent Leveraging Massive Unannotated Screenshots
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: GUICrafter first learns grounding from large collections of unannotated screenshots and webpages, then uses a smaller high-quality dataset for reinforcement-learning calibration. The curriculum targets reduced dependence on manually annotated GUI training data.

name: One Forward Beats Two: InnerZoom for Accurate and Efficient GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: InnerZoom preserves target-region cues from intermediate decoder layers and reinjects a compact evidence state during coordinate decoding. Its single-forward GUI grounder is compared with crop-and-rerun zooming and matched supervised/RL baselines for accuracy and inference cost.

name: LUMOS: A Semantic Operating-System Layer for Accessibility-Grounded AI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: LUMOS converts native accessibility metadata and browser UI structure into semantic interface blueprints with stable element identifiers and available actions. It combines live pointer-to-element grounding with an observe-act loop constrained to visible-UI primitives.

name: DigitalCoach: Communication and Grounding Gaps in Human and Agentic Computer Use Coaching
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: DigitalCoach records expert–novice software coaching conversations aligned with screen and input events. Automated and interactive evaluations examine how model coaches differ from humans in explanation, error diagnosis and visual grounding when helping a learner operate software.

name: MAG: A Web-Agent Benchmark and Harness for Multimodal Action and Guide Generation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: MAG jointly evaluates browser task actions and user-facing guides grounded in screenshots through element marks or pixel coordinates. Its harness covers annotation, live evaluation and joint metrics, with an expert-trajectory-augmented GRPO training study.

name: Tactile: Giving Computer-Using Agents Hands and Feet
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Tactile turns accessibility, OCR and visual evidence into explicit desktop targets with executable actions and verification cues. Its execution loop chooses semantic actions or coordinate fallbacks while retaining provenance for replay and diagnosis.

name: Teach it to stop, not just to click
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The repair study uses five oracle-graded environments; task-level transfer is reported for a case where one corrective action remains.
summary: Studies verifier-guided repair of a 35B computer-use agent across five environments, examining variation across runs and data draws in done detection, GUI clicks, and field entry.

name: StepX-Edge: An On-Device UI Vision-Language Model via Architecture-Training-Deployment Co-Design
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces StepX-Edge, an on-device UI vision-language model for screen understanding, OCR, question answering, and element grounding on mobile chips.

name: MAGA: Multi-Platform Self-Fusion of GUI Agents via Structured Action Distillation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: MAGA distills specialized GUI agents into one policy by allocating supervision according to structured-action correctness. A training-only teacher hint supports fusion across mobile, web and desktop settings without changing student inputs.

name: GUI-Lens: Coarse-to-Fine Cropping for GUI Grounding with General-Purpose VLMs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: GUI-Lens uses OCR and detected interface components as coordinate references while a general-purpose VLM selects progressively enlarged screenshot crops. Instruction-conditioned checks constrain the crop and click proposals before mapping the final location back to the original screen.

name: MissClick: Execution-Aware Adversarial Attacks on Coordinate Generation in GUI Grounding Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: MissClick designs white-box attacks around the numerical effect of coordinate digits on executable GUI clicks. Separate untargeted displacement and targeted place-weighted objectives are evaluated across desktop, web and mobile grounding settings.

name: Hallucination-Free GUI Grounding via Regression-Free Layout-Aware Matching
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This framework separates frozen-model instruction expansion from a trained layout-aware matcher that localizes GUI elements without coordinate regression. Binary text/icon supervision supports the matcher, with evaluations on GUI grounding and Mind2Web element-selection tasks.

name: LookAgain: Closed-Loop GUI Grounding with Visually Grounded Reflection
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: LookAgain treats a GUI coordinate as a revisable hypothesis, rendering its marker and a local screenshot patch before confirmation. Reflective supervised trajectories provide a cold start, followed by GRPO using terminal grounding correctness.

name: Test-Time Self-Evolving GUI Visual Grounding via Reflection-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces a Test-Time Self-Evolving framework for GUI grounding that explores unseen interfaces, reflects on predicted coordinates, and distills those reflections into the model.

name: Lexical Coupling in GUI Element Grounding: Sentence Embeddings Track Labels across Mobile and Web
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Studies whether text-embedding GUI grounding scores reflect semantic matching or recovery of visible labels. Same-screen ranking comparisons with lexical baselines expose differences between deployable fusion, oracle selection, and performance on label-poor targets.

name: GUI-Primitives: Diagnosing Spatial Reasoning Failures in Vision-Language GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces GUI-Primitives, a paired-instruction benchmark that changes a spatial relation while holding the screenshot and anchor fixed. Its diagnostics separate failure to localize either candidate from failure to choose the candidate satisfying the relation.

name: Iron: Intent-Aligned and Retrospective Dual Learning Framework for Enhancing Generalist Virtual Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces Iron, a GUI-agent training framework that aligns low-level actions with high-level intent using cycle-consistency rewards. It also repurposes failed trajectories through hindsight reconstruction and evaluates transfer to other digital tasks.

name: Are We There Yet? Assessing Computer-Use Agents for Blind Users' Accessible Interaction with Desktop Applications
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: A diary study deploys the screen-reader-accessible OLLA computer-use prototype with blind users across desktop applications. Recorded commands and interaction traces support model comparisons and analysis of grounding, planning, constraint tracking and termination failures.

name: CA-OPD: Confidence-Aware On-Policy Distillation for Structured Visual Prediction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). GUI grounding is one evaluated task alongside optical character recognition.
summary: Introduces CA-OPD, a confidence-guided distillation method for visual prediction, evaluated on GUI grounding and optical character recognition benchmarks.

name: Tail-Likelihood Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). GUI grounding is evaluated alongside object localization, maze navigation, and code optimization.
summary: Introduces Tail-Likelihood Reinforcement Learning (TailRL), an RL objective that favors rare high-reward rollouts; GUI grounding is one of several evaluation tasks.

name: LLaDA-UI: Bringing Block-wise Diffusion to Vision-Language GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: LLaDA-UI adapts block-wise diffusion generation to a vision-language GUI agent through multimodal pretraining and GUI supervised fine-tuning. It evaluates grounding and navigation across multiple platform settings.

name: Learning from Reliable Negatives: Confidence-Anchored Test-Time Adaptation for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Confidence-Anchored Learning uses coordinate-token confidence to filter pseudo-supervision for GUI grounding. Its negative-only variant performs label-free test-time updates to reduce reliance on potentially incorrect positive examples.

name: EchoPath: Execution-Level Replayable Memory for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: EchoPath turns validated GUI trajectories into parameterized replay procedures with explicit runtime preconditions. Image-based target matching adjusts stored coordinates, while ambiguous steps fall back to bounded repair or fresh planning.

name: RankGround: Efficient High-Resolution GUI Grounding via Lightweight Reranker-Guided Crop Selection
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: RankGround trains a lightweight reranker to select a promising screenshot crop before one VLM localization call. Ranking supervision uses containment and boundary-aware augmentation, with pointwise and listwise training stages.

name: MintAct: A Unified Visual Agent for Digital Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: MintAct trains a visual-agent family for grounding, navigation and tool use across mobile, desktop and web environments. Its shared infrastructure supports trajectory collection and asynchronous online RL while controlling cross-domain sampling and off-policy drift.

name: How Many Pixels Is a Digit Worth? Place-Aware Coordinate Entropy for GUI Agent Confidence Estimation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: PACE weights coordinate-digit entropy by place value to estimate confidence in GUI clicks from one forward pass. It evaluates correctness ranking and selective accuracy against repeated-sampling alternatives on ScreenSpot-Pro and ScreenSpot-v2.

name: Guides That Cause Actions: An Offline Study of Guide-Action Mutual Reinforcement in Multimodal Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: WebMRE pairs guidance sentences with grounded actions in an offline benchmark derived from successful WebArena traces. Controlled decoding-prefix interventions test how guide content affects action selection, while separating offline prediction metrics from live browser task success.

name: CaptchaArena: A Large-Scale, Fine-Grained Dataset for Training Computer-Use Agents on Interactive CAPTCHAs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces CaptchaArena, a dataset of execution-verified interactive CAPTCHA solutions with screenshot–action trajectories, reasoning annotations, and pixel masks for irregular targets. The work trains a single policy across CAPTCHA types using supervised learning followed by verifier-reward reinforcement learning.

name: ScreenHaystack: Finding Blind Zones in GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Moves controlled target icons across high-resolution interfaces to diagnose spatial blind zones in grounding models and study targeted augmentation.

name: DashAct: A Progressive Diagnostic Benchmark for GUI Agents in Interactive Dashboard Analysis
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Diagnoses dashboard-agent failures by progressively restoring interaction context, next-action support, and visual target information within the same task.

name: Probe to Act: Elevating Browser-Use Agent via Active Visual Probing
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces Probe to Act, which lets browser agents request visual evidence linking DOM handles and screen regions before committing an operation. It retains selected interaction evidence as memory and studies both prompted use and distillation into open models.

name: SPECTRA: On-Device Cognitive Perturbation and Trajectory Analysis for Autonomous Edge-Cloud GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported performance and request rates use two specified edge-cloud model pairs.
summary: Introduces SPECTRA, an edge-cloud GUI grounding framework that uses visual perturbations and trajectory analysis to decide when to request a cloud model.

name: Structured Interaction, Visual Localization, and Robust Execution for Complex Web Tasks: A Technical Report on the WebRetriever Challenge
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Describes a WebRetriever agent that combines semantic webpage operations with visual localization when structured representations are insufficient. Hierarchical context management and fault-aware execution support processing tasks across concurrent browsers.

name: SCA: Spatial Credit Assignment for Reinforcement Learning of GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces Spatial Credit Assignment, which uses click coordinates to refine group-relative reinforcement-learning updates for GUI grounding. It distinguishes failed clicks by spatial evidence while leaving the deployed action policy unchanged.

name: AutoGUIWorld: Image Generators as Visual World Models for GUI Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces AutoGUIWorld, which combines task planning and image editing to synthesize action-grounded GUI trajectories without running the depicted software. It filters generated transitions and tests whether training on them improves agents operating real desktop and scientific applications.

name: DeskForge: Dense Supervision from Desktop Environments for Computer-Use Agents
notes: Editorial summary based on the primary paper abstract.
summary: Generates dense desktop supervision by varying real application scenes and combining screenshots, accessibility trees, and window geometry.

name: Recurrent Latent Visual Search for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces ReLaViS, which performs recurrent visual search inside a grounding model by repeatedly querying screenshot tokens and feeding the resulting spatial evidence back into the model. Coarse-to-fine supervision is constructed from existing interface-element annotations.

name: Decoupling What from Where: How Should a Small GUI Grounding Model Receive the Action Type?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Compares ways to condition a small GUI grounding model on action type under matched training conditions on Android in the Wild. The study traces apparent gains to a coordinate-serialization choice and reports limited evidence that the gains persist with predicted action types.
